To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we constructed CD46 cytoplasmic tail-specific monoclonal antibody and used it to show that Cyt1 and 2 are recruited to different sites beneath N. gonorrhoeae microcolonies.
the CD46 Cyt1 and the Cyt2 tails have distinct roles in CD46 trafficking and signaling.

we constructed and tested two monoclonal antibodies specific to the cytoplasmic domains of CD46 and that we used these antibodies to study the recruitment of the two cytosolic tails of CD46 to the cortical plaque in Neisseria gonorrhea-infected cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of CD46 in the pathogenesis of gonococcal infections.
the molecular mechanisms that govern the recruitment of the two CD46 isoforms to the cortical plaque beneath the microcolonies of N. gonorrhoeae.
developing and applying novel molecular reagents to study the functions of CD46 isoforms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD46 tail-specific monoclonal antibody can be used for the immunofluorescent detection of Cyt1 or/and Cyt2 in the cell surface and the cell cytoplasm.
the CD46 tail-specific MAbs described here will be useful in studies of the role of the CD46 tails in cellular processes.
the Cyt1 and the Cyt2 tails are differentially recruited to the cortical plaque in response to N. gonorrhoeae infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD46 tail MAabs can be used to dissect the functions of CD46 cytoplasmic domains in signaling and trafficking.
we have generated MAbs that recognize unique regions of CD46 Cyt1 and CD46 Cyt2.
the Cyt1 and 2 MAbs will allow for the dissection of the functions of the Cyt1 versus Cyt2 tails in cellular processes such as signaling and trafficking.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have generated a panel of CD46 tail-specific MAbs that can be used to dissect the functions of the Cyt1 and the Cyt2 tails.
the Cyt1- specific MAb can be used to detect CD46 clustering in cells infected with N. gonorrhoeae, and this MAb will be a valuable tool for future studies of CD46 in infection and signaling.
the Cyt1- or Cyt2-specific MAbs can be used to study the functions of CD46 in innate and adaptive immune responses.
